tn.quote: Момбо – тональный язык с двумя простыми уровневыми тонами – высоким (H) и низким (L). В качестве минимального сегментного субстрата для простого тона (TBU, «tone bearing unit») выступает мора. Контурные тоны – восходящий (LH), нисходящий (HL) и восходяще-нисходящий (LHL) – образуются комбинацией простых тонов. Слоги, несущие контурные тоны, обязательно содержат две или более моры. Тоны используются для выражения как лексических, так и грамматических значений. … Каждое существительное обладает лексической тональной мелодией, которую оно несет в изолированном произношении.
tn.translation: Mombo is a tone language with two simple level tones, high (H) and low (L). The mora serves as the minimal segmental substrate for a simple tone (TBU). Contour tones, rising (LH), falling (HL) and rising-falling (LHL), are formed by combining simple tones. Syllables bearing contour tones obligatorily contain two or more morae. Tones are used to express both lexical and grammatical meanings. ... Every noun has a lexical tonal melody, which it carries when pronounced in isolation.

tn.note: Two level tones, high and low, the mora being the tone-bearing unit; rising, falling and rise-fall contours are H/L combinations on heavy syllables; nouns carry one of three melodies (H, HL, LH). tn.quote: Il existe deux tons de base: bas et haut; et deux doubles: montant et descendant. La tonalité respecte l'allure générale du N tant pour les nominaux, les verbaux que pour les pronominaux. Quelques mots invariables étant propres au lonkutsu ont une tonalité particulière. Ajoutons plutSt qu'il a été constaté de légères différences tonales entre Ie pa~Ier d'Ok~la ett celui de Ohambe … Mais en réalité, dans beaucoup de cas il s'agit dans les deux parlers d'un ton pausal, c'est-à-dire qu'à la limite de l'énoncé Ie ton haut est réalisé plus ou moins bas.
tn.translation: There are two basic tones: low and high; and two double (compound) ones: rising and falling. The tonality follows the general pattern of N [Lonkundo] for nominals, verbals and pronominals alike. A few invariable words peculiar to Lonkutsu have a particular tonality. Let us add rather that slight tonal differences have been noted between the Okala variety and that of Ohambe ... But in reality, in many cases what is involved in both varieties is a pausal tone, i.e. at the utterance boundary the high tone is realised more or less low.
tn.cite: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1989. Esquisse grammaticale du lonkutsu. Annales Aequatoria 10: 91-116.

tn.translation: In this investigation of the same variety, by contrast, 10 tones are found (3 level: B = low, M = mid, A = high, and 7 contour: AS, AM, AB, MA, MB, BA, BM, where S = super-high). … Among the level tones we find: low-low (BB), mid-mid (MM), high-high (AA) … For the rising tones we have low-mid (BM), low-high (BA), mid-high (MA), high-superhigh (AS) … For the falling tones we find high-low (AB), high-mid (AM), mid-low (MB) … The AB pattern occurs only in loans in the data collected.
tn.cite: Cruz López, Oswaldo. 2022. Cláusulas de relativo en el tu'un savi de Santo Tomás Ocotepec, Tlaxiaco, Oaxaca. Tesis de Maestría en Lingüística Indoamericana, CIESAS / INPI, Ciudad de México, enero 2022. ix+184 pp.

tn.note: Ten tonal patterns over the two-vowel couplet, from low, mid, high and a marginal super-high: level LL MM HH, rising LM LH MH H-superH, falling HM ML and HL (loans only); tone also marks verb aspect.

5580.prule: Family-level rule (Chapakura; Oro Win measured in sec. 5.2): accent is predictable from syllable weight, the only prosodic factor: a light syllable is unstressed and low-toned, the heavy syllable (CVC, CVː, CVV), which always stands lexeme-final with at most one light syllable before it, is stressed and high-toned, so stress is invariably lexeme-final.
5580.quote: Nas línguas Chapakura, a acentuação dos lexemas é dedutível do peso silábico - o único fator prosódico fonológico nessa família lingüística. Portanto, o acento não é fonológico por ser previsível. … (a) uma sílaba leve é átona e possui um tom baixo. … (b) uma sílaba pesada é tônica e possui um tom alto.
5580.loc: §2.2 p. 23 (restated §4.2.2 p. 68; Oro Win measurements §5.2 pp. 147-150)
5580.idn: Name in the source: Oro Win; family in the source: família lingüística Chapakura (language no. 05 in the author's list of Chapakura languages)

tn.quote: Nas línguas Chapakura, a acentuação dos lexemas é dedutível do peso silábico - o único fator prosódico fonológico nessa família lingüística. Portanto, o acento não é fonológico por ser previsível. … A atualização fonética da acentuação lexical obedece às seguintes regras: (a) uma sílaba leve é átona e possui um tom baixo. Em outras palavras, carrega um acento de intensidade (“stress”) fraco e um acento de altura (“pitch”) baixo; (b) uma sílaba pesada é tônica e possui um tom alto. Em outras palavras, carrega um acento de intensidade (“stress”) forte e um acento de altura (“pitch”) alto.
tn.translation: In the Chapakura languages, the accentuation of lexemes is deducible from syllable weight - the only phonological prosodic factor in this language family. Accent is therefore not phonological, being predictable. … The phonetic realisation of lexical accentuation obeys the following rules: (a) a light syllable is unstressed and has a low tone; in other words it carries a weak intensity accent ('stress') and a low pitch accent; (b) a heavy syllable is stressed and has a high tone; in other words it carries a strong intensity accent ('stress') and a high pitch accent.
tn.cite: Angenot, Geralda de Lima Vitor [= Angenot-de-Lima, Geralda]. 2013 [1997]. Fonotática e fonologia do lexema Protochapakura. Revista Eletrônica Língua Viva (Porto Velho: Universidade Federal de Rondônia), Série de e-books & e-documentos 2013, número 1 (= vol. 3, n. 1), 159 pp. ISSN 2237-9800. [E-book publication of the author's Dissertação de Mestrado, UNIR Guajará-Mirim, 1997.]
tn.locator: §2.2 'A estrutura prosódica do lexema', p. 23; Oro Win-specific: §5.2 conclusion (d) p. 149 and tables pp. 147-148, 150
tn.note: No lexical tone: accent is predictable from syllable weight (the final heavy syllable is stressed and high-pitched, light syllables low); pitch and intensity form one non-contrastive prominence.

tn.quote: Le pepel comporte 43 phonèmes répartis en 25 consonnes dont 7 prénasales et 18 voyelles (dont 10 brèves, 5 longues et 3 prénasales). La langue ne comporte pas de ton mais se caractérise par la présence d’un accent tonique qui tombe sur la voyelle de la première syllabe du lexème2.

5582.idn: Name in the source: pere (pɛrɛ); the language calls itself pɛr muurɛ̃ 'the language of the Pere people'; family in the source: famille adamaoua (Adamawa); related to dii (duru), nduupa, dooyayo

tn.quote: Le ton est significatif en pere. On trouve beaucoup de paires minimales où la seule différence entre les mots réside dans le ton. On compte trois tons distinctifs, même si l'on peut compter plusieurs hauteurs phonétiquement. … Le ton se manifeste sur les syllabes, c'est-à-dire que chaque syllabe a son propre ton, et doit toujours se prononcer à voix haute, moyenne ou basse. Lorsqu'il y a des exceptions, on en trouve l'explication dans des phénomènes d'intonation. Il existe par exemple des noms composés qui apparaissent avec un ton modulé.
tn.translation: Tone is significant in Pere. One finds many minimal pairs where the only difference between the words lies in the tone. One counts three distinctive tones, even if more pitch heights can be counted phonetically. … Tone is manifested on the syllables, that is, each syllable has its own tone and must always be pronounced at high, mid or low pitch. When there are exceptions, their explanation is found in intonation phenomena. There are for example compound nouns that appear with a modulated (contour) tone.
tn.cite: Raen, Konstanse. 1993. Les activités du centre de littérature pere. In: Adala, Hermenegildo & Boutrais, Jean (eds.), Peuples et cultures de l'Adamaoua (Cameroun): actes du colloque de Ngaoundéré du 14 au 16 janvier 1992, 225-234. Paris: ORSTOM / Ngaoundéré-Anthropos (Colloques et Séminaires). ISBN 2-7099-1167-1.
tn.locator: p. 228, section 'Les tons' (pp. 228-229)
tn.note: Three level tones (high, mid, low); each syllable carries its own tone. Contours only on some compound nouns and a predictable low-mid in CVN syllables; tone also marks verb transitivity.

tn.quote: The tonal system comprises 4 tones in non-checked syllables and 2 tones in checked syllables. … There are 4 tones in Phrae Pwo Karen, namely, the high tone, mid tone, low tone and falling tone with an allotone in the mid tone and falling tone. Phonetically, the high tone is high level and high rising [44 ~ 45], the mid tone is mid level [33], the low tone is low falling [21], and the falling tone is high falling [41]. The mid tone in checked syllables is [332 ~ 32] and the falling tone is [442 ~ 42].
